text.title: LLM-Friendly Architecture (Software Developer) — Worked Example
text.summary: One complete audit record for a React storefront edited daily by Claude Code — histogram, three oversized files with named splits, one depth violation, one barrel, one namespace import, naming score with offenders, inline data, CLAUDE.md at the same limit — with a note on each non-obvious value, then the audit as it is usually written (a 400-line limit, "split later", a score with no names) and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: acme/storefront, TypeScript and React, edited by Claude Code on most pull requests. Edits to `CheckoutPage.tsx` keep breaking the address form because the model never sees the bottom of the 1,412-line file. swe:alice runs `templates/llm-arch-audit.sh` on `a1b2c3d4e5f` with the default limit of 250.

example.title: storefront first audit
example.note: `line_limit` is 250, the script default, so this audit is comparable with the next one (r-file-size-histogram-with-threshold). `oversized[]` is sorted by lines and every `proposed_split` names target files, which is what separates a split from a `Foo2.tsx` (fm-01). The single `directory_depth` violation is 5 levels below `src` and the decision flattens it into one kebab-case feature folder (r-directory-depth-cap). `barrels[]` and the namespace import in `SearchPanel.tsx` come first in the decision because they hide symbol locations for every other finding (r-no-barrel-reexports, r-explicit-imports-no-wildcards); `react` and `three` are on the allow-list so their namespace imports are not hits. `naming.score` 84 is accompanied by the two offenders, each with a new name (r-naming-clarity-score-lists-offenders). `inline_data[]` shows the 214-line menu array inside `CheckoutPage.tsx`, the cheapest 214 lines to remove (r-static-data-extracted-from-components). `claude_md.line_limit` equals the input, so the agent will read the same number the audit enforces (r-claude-md-matches-audit). `evidence[]` carries the command and the SHA; `ci_wired` is false because the baseline is not yet clean, and the decision ends with wiring CI (r-audit-is-reproducible-command).

example.title: the audit as it is usually written
example.note: What the validator prints: `line_limit` 400 is above the maximum of 300 (r-file-size-histogram-with-threshold); `proposed_split` "split later" is too short and names no file (fm-01); `naming.score` 71 with empty `offenders[]` (r-naming-clarity-score-lists-offenders); `decision` names no file (r-file-size-histogram-with-threshold); `evidence[]` has one entry and neither an audit command nor a SHA (r-audit-is-reproducible-command); `claude_md.line_limit` 250 does not equal the input 400 (r-claude-md-matches-audit, cross-field). What the reviewer sees: a barrel listed but not deleted, so the next agent session opens `index.ts` and finds nothing (fm-02).
